modelResponse.episodeSummary: Thomas B. Nguyen, 55M, post-op day 1, experiencing multifocal PVCs and non-sustained VT, hemodynamically stable.
keyECGEvidence: Morphology: Sinus beats with multifocal wide PVCs, couplets, one non-sustained VT run of 4 beats
Pre-event note: Post-op, on thiazide; PVC burden increasing over last hour
modelResponse.mechanism: Hypokalemia and Hypomagnesemia increase ventricular automaticity and excitability, leading to premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) and potentially ventricular tachycardia (VT).
contributingFactors: Hydrochlorothiazide use (diuretic causing potassium and magnesium loss)

rejectedAlternatives.why: No significant ST deviation reported. Troponin T is mildly elevated, likely post-operative, not critically high. No chest pain or other signs of ischemia are mentioned.
Patient is not on digoxin. No signs of digoxin toxicity (e.g., bradycardia, specific ECG changes like scooped ST segments) are present.

Patient has mild diastolic dysfunction, but no known significant structural heart disease is mentioned. While this could be a factor, the acute change and electrolyte abnormalities point more strongly to an electrolyte etiology.

recommendedActions: Administer IV Potassium Chloride (e.g., 20 mEq in 100 mL NS over 1 hour, monitor ECG and K+ levels)
Administer IV Magnesium Sulfate (e.g., 2g IV over 10-20 minutes, monitor reflexes and BP)
Obtain repeat electrolytes (K+, Mg++, Ca++) in 1-2 hours
Consider cardiology consult if ectopy persists or worsens despite electrolyte correction
